text:
Alisha: quick handoff — I'm leaving at 18:30 UTC, leaving Mike as primary and Rajesh as secondary for the next 8h window. Leaving notes below.

Mike: got it. are there any active incidents or customer-facing issues i should prioritize?

Alisha: no live P0s right now. small flattening of hosted-api success rate earlier (brief spike at 16:10 UTC) — resolved by automatic fallback to model-variant v2-qual. check the observability dashboard if you see new spikes.

Rajesh: noted. any coverage gaps we need to call out?

Alisha: yes — coverage gap between 22:00–23:00 UTC because Erin is out and we don't have a third on-call. If something high-impact hits during that hour, escalate straight to the ENG-SRE manager and ping the oncall rotation channel.

Erin: thanks for the heads-up — I'm reachable by DM until 20:00 UTC if anything needs quick context before I go offline.

SRE-bot: Incident watch started for channel eng-oncall. Monitoring rules: API error-rate > 2% for 5m, latency p95 > 800ms for 10m, model-serve queue depth > 300.

Mike: for paging rules, confirm: page primary first, wait 5m, page secondary, wait 10m, then escalate to ENG-SRE manager + eng-lead?

Alisha: yes — that's the current policy. Condensed: page primary (PD, push & SMS). If no ACK in 5m, page secondary. If no ACK within 15 total minutes or any P0 customer-impacting outage, escalate immediately to Eng Manager (pager + @channel) and open a bridge.

Rajesh: what about functional ownership? for capacity / runtime crashes, who should we page first: eng-runtime or infra?

Alisha: rule of thumb: runtime-level errors (OOM, core dumps, worker crashes) -> eng-runtime team first. Infra (instance provisioning, network) -> eng-infra/SRE. If it's unclear, page both on the 2nd escalation. Example: if GPU nodes are failing and runtime logs show model process OOMs, start with eng-runtime and include eng-infra after 5m if not progressing.

SRE-bot: Paging template ready: 
```
Subject: P0 - <short impact> - <service>
Who: Primary oncall @<name>
What: brief symptom & observed metrics
Where: region / environment
Action: immediate mitigation attempts & link to runbook
```
Alisha: runbooks to bookmark: OpsRunbook -> /runbooks/production/paging-and-escalation, Runtime -> /runbooks/serving/runtime-crash, DB -> /runbooks/storage/pg-replication. OpsRunbook-bot can link the exact anchor if you ask.

OpsRunbook-bot: Quick links: /runbooks/production/paging-and-escalation, /runbooks/serving/runtime-crash, /runbooks/storage/pg-replication.

Mike: customer impact assessment guidance? need to know when to call support/product and notify customers.

Alisha: use the customer-impact checklist in the escalation runbook. Short rules: if >5% requests for a customer fail for >10min OR any customer SLA breach (>=99.9% contract) -> notify product & support immediately and draft a status page draft. For degraded latency (p95 >2x baseline) evaluate with product on messaging.

Rajesh: for a quick checklist to share with whoever picks up: 1) Confirm scope (global or region), 2) Attach latest traces/logs, 3) Confirm rollback/fallback options, 4) Decide contact list (support/product/ops).

Mike: adding that to my notes. ack windows: should we shorten the wait for broad customer-impacting incidents?

Alisha: yes — if you see clear customer-impacting telemetry (errors, billing spikes, downstream queues growing), treat as immediate P0 and escalate to managers at T+5 if no ack. No waiting for full 15m in those cases.

Erin: what's the preferred channel for the post-incident blameless summary? eng-oncall or incidents?

Alisha: initial triage updates in eng-oncall during incident. After the incident, move the blameless postmortem to sources/incidents/ and mention eng-oncall thread in the postmortem draft. Use the incident template in /templates/incident-postmortem.

SRE-bot: Reminder: annotate the incident with severity and customer-impact tags when creating the bridge.

Mike: any quick mitigations I should be comfortable doing before looping others? e.g., temporary model fallback, scale-up, or drain nodes?

Alisha: approved immediate mitigations for oncall: 1) trigger model fallback to v1-compat if v2 shows regressions, 2) increase worker pool by 2x for 10–15m to drain backlog (watch cost), 3) restart single failing worker (not full cluster) if logs show OOM for that PID. Always document actions in the incident thread.

Rajesh: documented. if i page eng-runtime and they ask for logs, what's the standard snippet to pull?

Alisha: use this snippet: 
```
# collect last 2k lines of worker logs
journalctl -u redwood-worker -n 2000 --no-pager > /tmp/worker-logs.txt
# top mem processes
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 20
```
Attach /tmp/worker-logs.txt to the incident bridge.

Mike: corner case — scheduled maintenance overlapping this shift (db rollover at 22:15 UTC). how do we handle paging during maintenance?

Alisha: maintenance windows should be in the maintenance calendar and we should annotate any pages during that time with "maintenance" if expected. If the symptom exceeds expected maintenance side effects (e.g., >2x expected error budget), treat as incident. If maintenance causes customer impact, follow escalation normally.

Erin: i'll remind the SRE manager about the 22:00 coverage gap in the weekly rota so we can avoid repeating.

Mike: thanks — i'm on it. final ack from me, i'm primary and reachable on PD/SMS.

Rajesh: secondary acked.

Alisha: thanks team — leaving now. tag me if anything urgent. :wave:
